title: Well-defined poset structure on the induced space G ×^P X'
body_html:
Well-defined poset structure on the induced space

Fix the induction data $(G', P)$ satisfying (P0)–(P2) and the induced space $X = G \times^P X'$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]].

The face relation on $X$ is not automatic from the definition of $X$ as a set-theoretic quotient — it must be extracted from a candidate relation on the representative product $G \times X'$ and shown to descend to the quotient by $\sim$.

Candidate relation on representatives

Define $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$ by

$$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \;:\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\;\; n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \;\text{in } X' \;\text{and}\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. $$

Compare with the equivalence relation $$ (g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, E_2) \;:\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\;\; n \cdot E_1 = E_2 \;\text{and}\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}, $$ which is the special case with the face relation $\preceq$ replaced by equality.

Well-definedness

Proposition (poset structure on $G \times^P X'$). Under (P0)–(P2), $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ satisfies:

  1. Reflexivity. $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g, E)$.
  2. Transitivity. $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$ imply $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$.
  3. Left descent. If $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ then $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F) \iff (g_1', E_1') \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$.
  4. Right descent. If $(h, F) \sim (h', F')$ then $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F) \iff (g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h', F')$.
  5. Antisymmetry modulo $\sim$. If both $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_1, E_1)$, then $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, E_2)$.

Consequently, the relation $$[(g_1, E_1)] \preceq [(g_2, E_2)] > \;:\iff\; > (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$$ is a well-defined partial order on $G \times^P X'$.
proof_html:
(1) Reflexivity. Take $n := 1 \in G'$. Then $1 \cdot E = E \preceq E$ and $g^{-1} g \cdot 1 = 1 \in P_E$.

(2) Transitivity. Given witnesses $n_1$ for $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $n_2$ for $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$, take $n := n_2 n_1 \in G'$. Face-chain: $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = n_2 \cdot (n_1 \cdot E_1) \preceq n_2 \cdot E_2 \preceq E_3$ using cellularity ($n_2$ preserves $\preceq$) and transitivity of $\preceq$.

The membership $g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) \in P_{E_1}$ is the technical core. From the hypotheses $g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$ and $g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{E_2}$:

  • By (P0) and $n_1 \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$: $P_{E_2} \le P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$, so $g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$.
  • By (P1): $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} = n_1 P_{E_1} n_1^{-1}$, so there exists $p \in P_{E_1}$ with $n_1 p n_1^{-1} = g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2$.
  • Rearranging: $g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) = (g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1) \cdot p \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$.

(3) Left descent. Suppose $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ with witness $m \in G'$: $m \cdot E_1 = E_1'$ and $g_1^{-1} g_1' m \in P_{E_1}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := n m^{-1} \in G'$.

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E_1' = n m^{-1} \cdot (m \cdot E_1) = n \cdot E_1 \preceq F$.
  • Membership: write $g_1^{-1} g_1' m = \alpha \in P_{E_1}$. Compute $(g_1')^{-1} h n'' = m \alpha^{-1} g_1^{-1} h n m^{-1}$; substitute $g_1^{-1} h n \in P_{E_1}$ and use (P1) with $m$ to conclude $m \alpha^{-1} (g_1^{-1} h n) m^{-1} \in m P_{E_1} m^{-1} = P_{m \cdot E_1} = P_{E_1'}$.

The reverse implication is symmetric via $m^{-1}$.

(4) Right descent. Suppose $(h, F) \sim (h', F')$ with witness $m$. Assume $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := m n \in G'$.

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E = m \cdot (n \cdot E) \preceq m \cdot F = F'$.
  • Membership: write $h^{-1} h' m = \alpha \in P_F$. By (P0) with $n \cdot E \preceq F$: $\alpha \in P_F \le P_{n \cdot E}$. By (P1): $\alpha = n p n^{-1}$ for some $p \in P_E$. Compute $g^{-1} h' n'' = (g^{-1} h n) \cdot p$; both factors lie in $P_E$.

(5) Antisymmetry modulo $\sim$. From $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ via $n_1$ and the reverse via $n_2$, we obtain $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 \preceq E_1$. Because the $G$-action is cellular it preserves dimension (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex): $\dim((n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1) = \dim E_1$. Strict monotonicity of $\dim$ along a proper face-chain (Abstract cell complex) then forces $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = E_1$, hence $n_1 \cdot E_1 = E_2$ (and the $P_{E_1}$-membership from the $n_1$-witness is exactly the $\sim$-witness).

Descent packaging. Clauses (3) + (4) give bivariate descent of $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ through $\sim$ on both arguments, so the quotient carries a well-defined relation $\preceq$. Clauses (1) + (2) transport to $\preceq$ verbatim; clause (5) makes $\preceq$ antisymmetric on the quotient. Thus $\preceq$ is a partial order on $G \times^P X'$. $\square$

Consequences

  • The embedding $\iota : X' \to G \times^P X'$, $E \mapsto [(1, E)]$, is order-preserving and order-reflecting; this is ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (2), now supported by a genuine partial-order structure on the target.
  • The dimension function $\dim([(g, E)]) := \dim E$ is well-defined because $\sim$ implies dimension-equal (from $n \cdot E_1 = E_2$ and dimension-preservation of the $G$-action).
  • Together with local finiteness of $X'$ (inherited via $G$-translates), this equips $G \times^P X'$ with the abstract-cell-complex and $G$-cell-complex instances that CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' uses as its poset-level content.

Which axioms feed into which clause

Clause Axioms used
(1) Reflexivity none (unit in $G'$, unit in $P_E$)
(2) Transitivity (P0), (P1)
(3) Left descent (P1)
(4) Right descent (P0), (P1)
(5) Antisymmetry dimension preservation (cellular action), strict monotonicity

(P2) does not enter this proposition; it enters the equivalence (as opposed to face) relation via ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (1) (injectivity of $\iota$).

Lean formalization

The representative relation is InductionDatum.leRep : G × X' → G × X' → Prop:

def leRep (g₁E₁ g₂E₂ : G × X') : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • g₁E₁.2 ≤ g₂E₂.2 ∧
              g₁E₁.1⁻¹ * g₂E₂.1 * n ∈ d.P g₁E₁.2

The five clauses correspond to

Clause Lean lemma
(1) leRep_refl
(2) leRep_trans
(3) leRep_left_descends
(4) leRep_right_descends
(5) leRep_antisymm

The PartialOrder instance on InducedSpace d is built by Quotient.lift₂ (leRep d) — clauses (3) + (4) discharge the well-definedness side condition of Quotient.lift₂; clauses (1) + (2) discharge reflexivity and transitivity of the descended le; clause (5) discharges antisymmetry.

instance : PartialOrder (InducedSpace d) where
  le := Quotient.lift₂ (leRep d) ⟨left/right descent + symm/inv⟩
  le_refl  := ⟨leRep_refl⟩
  le_trans := ⟨leRep_trans⟩
  le_antisymm := ⟨leRep_antisymm⟩

The dimension function InducedSpace.dim and the AbstractCellComplex (InducedSpace d) / GCellComplex G (InducedSpace d) instances stack on top of this PartialOrder.
